model.rationale: DeSaulnier holds a heavily Democratic seat, has out-raised his little-known Republican opponent, and markets price him as an overwhelming favorite. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or unexpected outside spending against DeSaulnier would warrant a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. He advanced to the general election and has raised about $567,000 with nearly $586,000 on hand, while Republican Jeff Frese has reported little in the way of fundraising or outside support. Prediction markets put DeSaulnier's chances at roughly 96 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and market pricing. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with low risk of an upset.
